blocks.text: Pacific Douglas, South Surrey: Neighbourhood Guide
Living in Pacific Douglas, South Surrey

parts.t: Pacific Douglas is the MLS® sub-area at the southern edge of South Surrey, against the United States border. At its centre is Douglas, which the City calls its most southern urban neighbourhood, set between the Peace Arch and Pacific Highway crossings. Its plan covers about 61 hectares, with farmland in the Agricultural Land Reserve and the Glades garden on its north side. Border traffic, the ALR edge and the age of the subdivision are worth looking at before you buy.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations and school catchments before you buy or sell.

parts.t: The Douglas plan is complete and now sits under the OCP, with the ALR on its north side.
Council approved the Stage 1 Douglas land use plan in July 1996 and the Stage 2 plan in July 1999 (Corporate Report C429).
Douglas’s land use designations are now superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP, but the plan still guides public amenities and infrastructure.
The plan area is bordered by the Agricultural Land Reserve and the Glades garden to the north.
The Peace Arch is a City heritage site and is listed on the Canadian Register of Historic Places.
